description: A two-panel, purely schematic line drawing (no axes, no scale bar, no numeric values) titled in the paper as a model of dislocation pile-up. Both panels are labelled at the left: (a) is the upper row and (b) the lower row. Each panel depicts a horizontal dashed line on which sit five black T-shaped dislocation symbols, and the two rows are drawn one above the other for direct comparison. A large open block arrow at the top, labelled with the Greek letter tau (τ), points to the right and denotes the applied shear stress. At the right-hand end of both dashed lines a vertical wavy line is labelled "Grain boundary", marking the obstacle against which the dislocations are stopped. Four dotted arrows run from individual dislocations in (a) down to the corresponding positions in (b), indicating the change in dislocation position/configuration between the two states. The panels make one argument together: dislocations driven by τ travel along their slip line and pile up against the grain boundary in (a), and the (b) configuration shows the resulting retained/redistributed arrangement of those dislocations. No magnitudes, grain sizes or distances are printed anywhere in the figure; it is qualitative.

subfigures.description: Upper schematic row: five black T-shaped dislocation symbols distributed along a horizontal dashed slip line, with the applied shear-stress arrow τ above them and the wavy 'Grain boundary' line at the right end. Represents dislocations moving under τ and piling up at the boundary.

Lower schematic row: the same dashed slip line with black T-shaped dislocation symbols, connected to panel (a) by four dotted correspondence arrows, showing the dislocation arrangement after the pile-up/displacement. Same 'Grain boundary' wavy line at the right.

observations.observation: Both panels consist of a horizontal dashed slip line carrying five black T-shaped dislocation symbols, drawn as a before/after pair labelled (a) and (b).
A large open block arrow labelled 'τ' at the top of the figure points rightward, indicating the applied shear stress acting on the dislocations.
A vertical wavy line at the right-hand end of both dashed lines is labelled 'Grain boundary', identifying the obstacle at which dislocations are blocked.
Four dotted arrows connect dislocations in (a) to their counterparts in (b), showing the change in dislocation position between the two configurations.
The figure contains no axes, no scale bar, no legend and no printed numeric values; it is a qualitative mechanism schematic.
The caption states the figure is a 'Model of dislocation pile-up'.
The citing text states that pile-up causes deformation during unloading and also during loading at a stress even smaller than the yield stress.
The citing text states that movable dislocations lower the apparent elastic modulus, and that this decrease grows as a function of plastic strain.

The citing text states that dislocation pile-up is considered to occur near grain boundaries, so movable dislocations are more likely there than in other partitions, making apparent elastic moduli differ from boundary to centre of the grain.
